coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 6 directories containing an *-index.md (the domain root plus 10.01-10.05), 40 files total - exactly the expected counts. Every one of the 40 files was read in full (the eight largest, 50-88 KB each, were read in sequential slices). Rubric dimensions 4 (Constraint Explicitness), 5 (Success Measurability) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are marked N/A for every unit: constraints, success metrics and competitor analysis live in .memory/wiki/specs/ideation/meta/ (constraints.md, competitive-landscape.md), which is outside this domain's scope and is never restated in domain 10. Dimensions 1, 2, 3, 7 and 8 are applicable to all six units (5 applicable checkpoints per unit, 30 total). Sub-domain CX files at [SURFACE] status detail only a subset of their mapped edges (e.g. 10.01-cx details 3 of 8); this is disclosed by the declared status rather than hidden, so it is not scored as a structural failure. Many apparent contradictions were tested and dropped on the devil's-advocate pass because they are stale parent-CX framings that a deepened child has already resolved (royalties-collections-cx.md CX-06 Q4 and 10.04-cx CX-02 Q4 both still call 10.04.03 DT-02 'unresolved' after 10.04.03 Q-03 resolved it; 10.02.05 Q-04 still says the registry lacks a remittee and correction window after 10.02.01 D-06/D-16 added both), or because the tracked-deferral rule covers them (10.02.04 Q-05 explicitly tracks the FX carve-out conflict with 10.02.02 D-02; 10.03.02 Q-05 explicitly tracks the Must-depends-on-Could gap with 10.08).

findings.claim: 10.02.01's `Overdue` state is specified to route unconditionally to 10.05.03 as a leakage finding, but the same file (a) enumerates three causes of silence and rules that only one of them is leakage, (b) states the platform cannot distinguish that cause from the modal 'user never uploaded the file' cause without a notification or the file, and (c) provides no state at all for that modal cause. The state machine therefore cannot satisfy its own constraint, and an implementer must invent either a discriminator the file says does not exist or a routing rule the file forbids.
findings.evidence: 10.02.01-statement-source-ingestion.md:258 (States) - '| **Overdue** | Calendared cycle passed, nothing arrived, **and the cross-user signal says the source distributed** | **A finding** (`D-02`, `D-14`) - money-denominated, dated, routed to `10.05.03` |'; contradicted by 10.02.01-statement-source-ingestion.md:112 (three causes of overdue) - '| **The source distributed, paid the user, and the file never reached the platform** | The user did not upload it. The modal case | The user | **No.** A nag. |'; and by 10.02.01-statement-source-ingestion.md:296 (Cross-Cut Notes) - '`DT-09` narrows what it may consume: of three causes of silence, only *"the source distributed and paid nothing"* is leakage. A slipped cycle is noise (`D-14`) and an un-uploaded file is a nag. Feeding all three through would poison the domain's highest-confidence detector with the domain's noisiest signal.'; with the impossibility stated at 10.02.01-statement-source-ingestion.md:279 (DT-09) - 'the platform cannot distinguish (b) from (c) alone - both look like silence from inside one user's account. It needs either the notification (`D-13`) or the file.' The edge-case table repeats the unconditional routing at 10.02.01-statement-source-ingestion.md:195 - 'Overdue against the source's cycle, denominated and dated, routed to `10.05.03`.'
findings.forcedInvention: For a calendared source where the cross-user signal says the source distributed, no notification was forwarded and no file was uploaded, the implementer must invent whether the platform (a) raises a money-denominated leakage finding to 10.05.03 (following the States and Edge Cases tables, knowingly poisoning the detector the file says must not be poisoned), (b) raises only a nag and never a finding (following DT-09 and the Cross-Cut Notes, silently deleting the feature's headline output for every user who does not forward notifications), or (c) invents a third state and a discriminator between causes (b) and (c) that DT-09 states does not exist.

findings.claim: 10.08 states that for a dispute about an ingested third-party statement the platform has no power and 'it stops', while its own States table and Happy Path hold the disputed amount in escrow for 'any live dispute'. Because an ingested label/distributor line still feeds calculation and downstream per-payee disbursement, whether a third-party-statement dispute freezes the platform-computed money owed to co-payees is unstated and untracked, and 10.04.04 lists 'a statement is challenged (10.08)' as an escrow trigger without distinguishing the two flows.
findings.evidence: 10.08-statement-disputes-audit-rights.md:29 (Behavior) - 'The platform can say *"our expectation was £X, your statement says £Y"* - which is genuinely more than the artist had before - and then it stops. It has no standing, no access, and no power.'; contradicted by 10.08-statement-disputes-audit-rights.md:62 (States) - '| Held | Any live dispute | `10.04.04` escrow |', by 10.08-statement-disputes-audit-rights.md:38 (Happy Path 4) - 'If not, the dispute engine runs it (cross-cut); the disputed amount is held (`10.04.04`)', and by 10.08-statement-disputes-audit-rights.md:93 (D-05) - 'Disputed amounts are **held**, not paid to either side | `10.04.04` D-01. Paying is a verdict.' The escrow feature inherits the ambiguity at 10.04-disbursement-payee-statements/10.04.04-disputed-royalty-escrow.md:10 - 'A split is disputed (domain 09), a credit is contested (`02.05`), a statement is challenged (`10.08`)' - with no distinction between a platform-issued statement and an ingested one. 10.08 D-02 (line 90) explicitly separates the two flows for every other purpose: 'Our statements and their statements are different flows'.
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must decide whether opening a dispute against an ingested third-party statement holds the platform-computed downstream disbursements derived from that statement's lines (freezing a co-payee's undisputed-to-them share) or holds nothing at all - a decision about whose money moves, taken with no rule in either file.

findings.claim: The payout threshold has two mutually exclusive owners in the same unit: the Role Lens and the sub-domain Role Matrix give threshold configuration to the administering Producer (the payer side), while D-04 and DT-03 say the threshold should be the payee's to set. 'Ideally' is not a decision, no default is stated, no precedence rule exists for the two parties disagreeing, and no open question tracks it - in a feature whose own DT-03 says the two parties' interests are opposed.
findings.evidence: 10.04.03-thresholds-holds-unpayable-balances.md:20 (Role Lens) - '| Producer | Config | Threshold policy on entities they administer, and - more consequentially - visibility of money owed to people who are **not on the platform** |', repeated at 10.04-disbursement-payee-statements-index.md:35 (Role Matrix) - '| 10.04.03 Thresholds, Holds & Unpayable Balances | 👁️ Read-only (own held money and why) | ⚙️ Config (threshold policy on entities they administer) |'; contradicted by 10.04.03-thresholds-holds-unpayable-balances.md:99 (D-04) - 'The **threshold is visible and justified**; ideally the payee's to set | DT-03. There is no neutral value, and the platform's interest opposes the payee's.' and by 10.04.03-thresholds-holds-unpayable-balances.md:81 (DT-03) - 'the honest handling is to make the threshold **visible, justified, and ideally the payee's to set** - the last of which nobody in the industry does.' The feature's three open questions (lines 106-108) cover permanently unpayable balances, client-money custody, and the resolved non-user message; none covers threshold ownership.
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent (a) whether the payout threshold is a payer/administrator setting or a payee setting, (b) which wins when both are set, and (c) the default value - each of which decides whose money is withheld and for how long, in the feature the domain names as its own black box.

findings.claim: 10.09 makes 'tolerance before alarming' a load-bearing decision (D-05) and puts it in the Overdue state's trigger, but the tolerance is never given a value, a derivation, a per-source anchor, or a tracked owner - unlike every sibling clock in the domain, each of which is anchored to a declared external window with a labelled fallback. The number decides when a leakage finding fires, and the file itself says false leakage findings are worse than having no calendar.
findings.evidence: 10.09-distribution-calendar-money-in-flight.md:52 (Edge Cases) - '| Distribution late | Societies slip | Tolerance before alarming; a slipped distribution is not a leak |'; 10.09-distribution-calendar-money-in-flight.md:66 (States) - '| Overdue | Past the distribution date + tolerance | → `10.05.03` finding |'; 10.09-distribution-calendar-money-in-flight.md:95 (D-05) - '| D-05 | Late ≠ leaked | Societies slip. Tolerance before alarm, or the feature cries wolf and gets muted. |'. The stakes are stated at 10.09-distribution-calendar-money-in-flight.md:101 (Q-01) - 'A stale calendar produces false leakage findings, which is worse than no calendar' - but Q-01 asks only who maintains the calendar, Q-02 is resolved, and Q-03 concerns receivables financing. Contrast the sibling clocks, which are all anchored: 10.02.05-unmatched-line-exception-queue.md:315 (D-17) - 'The clock is anchored to the **source's declared correction window** (`10.02.01` registry). An undeclared window is a **finding**, and the platform's 12-month fallback is **labelled as the platform's deadline, not the source's**'; and 10.01.03-cwr-society-file-exchange.md:87 (D-03) - 'Every submission carries an **expected-by date**; silence past it is an alarm', whose unknown-turnaround case is tracked at 10.01.04 Q-01 with Owner + target.
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent the tolerance window (a global constant? per society? per income type? derived from observed slip history?) that separates 'a society slipped' from 'a leakage finding routed to 10.05.03' - the single number that decides the false-positive rate of the domain's advertised detector.

findings.claim: 10.10 makes silence-on-thin-data its central honesty guarantee (D-03) and makes 'a range, never a point figure' its output contract (D-02), but neither the sufficiency threshold that triggers silence nor the confidence level the range is stated at is defined anywhere, and no open question covers either. Two implementers reading this file produce materially different products - one where most users see a range, one where almost none do.
findings.evidence: 10.10-royalty-forecasting.md:36 (Happy Path 1) - 'A catalogue has **enough distribution history to be statistically meaningful**'; 10.10-royalty-forecasting.md:38 (Happy Path 3) - 'Beyond it, a **range** with a stated confidence, derived from history and velocity'; 10.10-royalty-forecasting.md:59 (States) - '| Insufficient data | Thin history | **No forecast.** The most common and most honest state |'; 10.10-royalty-forecasting.md:88 (D-03) - '| D-03 | **Silence on thin data** | DT-01. Most users are unforecastable, and no forecast beats a fabricated one. |'. The three open questions (lines 97-99) are: Q-01 resolved (MoSCoW placement), Q-02 (whether domain 23 lending changes whether this ships at all), Q-03 resolved (in-flight ships first) - none defines the threshold or the confidence level. The edge case at line 47 restates the problem without resolving it: 'Ranges must be wide enough to be useless-looking, which is honest.'
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent (a) the quantity of distribution history that makes a catalogue forecastable, (b) the confidence level the published range represents, and (c) the width rule for 'wide enough to be useless-looking' - the three parameters that decide whether D-03's silence guarantee protects most users or almost none.

findings.claim: The domain index - the pipeline key file downstream stages read first - carries per-child depth metadata that contradicts the children's own headers: two leaf features are listed [SURFACE] while their files declare [PARTIAL], the classification note asserts every child is [SURFACE] while the same table lists [BREADTH] and [DEEP] children, and three sub-domains' hypothesis counts are the pre-deepening figures (10.02 is listed at 15 against its children's actual 68). A reader cannot determine from the key file which children have been deepened.
findings.evidence: royalties-collections-index.md:37 - '| 10.06 | Live Performance Setlist → PRO Reporting | feature | [10.06-live-setlist-pro-reporting.md](./10.06-live-setlist-pro-reporting.md) | `[SURFACE]` | 3 hypotheses |' contradicted by 10.06-live-setlist-pro-reporting.md:5 - '> **Status**: [PARTIAL]'. royalties-collections-index.md:40 - '| 10.09 | Distribution Calendar & Money-in-Flight | feature | ... | `[SURFACE]` | 3 hypotheses |' contradicted by 10.09-distribution-calendar-money-in-flight.md:5 - '> **Status**: [PARTIAL]'. royalties-collections-index.md:28 - 'All `[SURFACE]`.' contradicted by the immediately following table, which lists 10.01/10.03/10.04/10.05 as `[BREADTH]` and 10.02 as `[DEEP]`. royalties-collections-index.md:33 - '| 10.02 | Statement Ingestion & Normalization | sub-domain | ... | `[DEEP]` | 15 hypotheses (5 children) |' contradicted by 10.02-statement-ingestion-normalization-index.md:20-24, whose five children carry 17 + 13 + 13 + 10 + 15 = 68 hypotheses; the same staleness applies to 10.03 (listed 12; children carry 13 + 13 + 3 + 3 = 32) and 10.05 (listed 9; children carry 12 + 3 + 3 = 18).
findings.forcedInvention: A downstream stage selecting which nodes still need deepening, or deciding how much specification depth to expect from a child, gets a different answer from the key file than from the child - with no rule stating which wins.
